audit.why: 46.39% over 360 games and the chart reflects it honestly — Warwick takes levels 2-3 and both item stages, Camille gets only the flat windows and level 6. The 'stay above 50% HP' framing is the correct organising idea for a lane against a drain bruiser whose kit is built around low-health targets.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text says to trade 'before his W (Blood Hunt) attack-speed steroid is online', treating it as something that simply switches on at a level.
audit.why: Blood Hunt is 80s at rank 1 and only reaches 40s at rank 5 — by far the longest basic-ability cooldown in either kit, longer than Camille's Hookshot by a factor of five. It is not a permanent state he acquires, it is a resource he spends, which makes it the single most punishable cooldown in the lane and completely changes how the early game should be played. The text treats a 80s cooldown as a passive.
audit.corrected: Blood Hunt restated as an 80s cooldown to bait and punish rather than a steroid to race.

audit.whatIsWrong: The fear is attributed to Blood Hunt twice — 'his W active fears you' (spikes[3].text) and 'his W active fear locks you down' (wants.foe[0]). Warwick's fear is Primal Howl, his E, which is never mentioned. Camille's R is written without its article.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Blood Hunt (W) is the sense-and-chase steroid against low-health targets; Primal Howl (E) reduces incoming damage and then fears nearby enemies, on 15s at rank 1 down to 11s. Merging them hides a 15s ability behind an 80s one and tells the reader to fear the wrong cooldown at the wrong time. Primal Howl's damage reduction is also why bursting a Warwick who has just howled fails, which nothing in the matchup explains.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl named as the E fear with its 15s and its damage reduction; Blood Hunt restored to its actual role.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Burst him before his R (Infinite Duress) suppress is available' and 'always keep your own E for the escape' give no durations.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110s at rank 1 falling to 70s, and Jaws of the Beast is 8s. A Warwick who has spent his ultimate is safe to fight for well over a minute — that is the actual window the level-6 advice is pointing at, and it is worth naming because it is long enough to plan a dive around.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Hookshot's landing knockup interrupts Infinite Duress.
audit.why: Riot flags Infinite Duress as a channel, and Hookshot knocks up enemy champions on landing — a displacement breaks the channel outright. Camille cannot use this on herself while suppressed, but it makes her one of the better answers to a Warwick who has committed his ultimate onto a teammate, and it is the highest-value thing her kit does in this matchup outside the 1v1. _missing-interactions.json flags it for this exact pairing.
audit.corrected: Written into wants.you[1] as a teammate-peel use for the E.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warwick's healing is named as the losing factor in six separate lines and Grievous Wounds appears nowhere.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress together — three sources of sustain. Against that, anti-heal is not a situational buy, it is the buy, and the matchup never says so.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds cue added to late.

edits.before: Your Q recast true-damage hit out-trades Warwick before his W (Blood Hunt) attack-speed steroid is online — poke and back off while his Q (Jaws of the Beast) heal is still small.
edits.after: Your Q recast true-damage hit out-trades Warwick while Blood Hunt's 80s is spent — poke and back off inside Jaws of the Beast's 8s, while its heal is still small.

edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum is your one clean kill window: arena-lock him off the wave so he gets no minion healing, and take it while his 110s Infinite Duress is spent.

edits.after: Warwick edges 4-5: your Hookshot wins the opener, but Primal Howl's 15s cuts your burst and fears you out of the follow-up.

edits.before: Level 1 belongs to Warwick — his passive Eternal Hunger already chunks and heals him on autos, so don't contest with only your Q point. At 2 you spike: land Q's first hit, hold ~1s, recast for the bonus true damage and move-speed burst, then walk off before his Q (Jaws of the Beast) heal pays him back. Keep every trade short and ABOVE 50% HP — the instant you dip low his Eternal Hunger healing amplifies off you, his W active can fear you, and a drain bruiser wins any drawn-out exchange.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to Warwick — Eternal Hunger already chunks and heals him on autos, so don't contest with only your Q point. At 2 you spike: land Q's first hit, hold ~1s, recast for the bonus true damage and move-speed burst, then walk off inside Jaws of the Beast's 8s before its heal pays him back. Keep every trade short and ABOVE 50% HP — the instant you dip low Eternal Hunger amplifies, Blood Hunt senses and chases you, and a drain bruiser wins any long exchange.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 tilt toward Warwick: your Q-into-W-slow and E-wall stun win the short burst, but his Q heal and W (Blood Hunt) move speed let him re-engage and out-sustain you, so don't sit in his range — burst and disengage. Level 6 is your stage. Hextech Ultimatum traps him in the arena where he can't kite, and if you pull him off the wave you can burst him before he gets R (Infinite Duress) off on you. Always keep your own E for the escape — getting suppressed at low HP into his amplified healing is exactly how this lane kills you.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 tilt toward Warwick: your Q-into-W-slow and Hookshot win the short burst, but Primal Howl's 15s cuts the damage and fears you off the follow-up, then Jaws of the Beast heals it back — so burst and disengage. Level 6 is your stage. The Hextech Ultimatum traps him off the wave with nothing to heal from, and his 110s Infinite Duress is the only real answer, so take the fight once it is spent. Getting suppressed at low HP into his amplified healing is exactly how this lane kills you.

edits.before: This is where Warwick takes over. At 2+ items his Q heal and lifesteal off your bar out-sustain your burst, and his R is a point-and-click suppress that locks you for his team if you dive first. Your job is to use E mobility and R isolation to pick a SQUISHY carry, not to 1v1 Warwick — you lose that straight drain duel once his sustain is online. Snowball lane and side-lane pressure early so the game closes before his scaling sustain outweighs your pick potential.
edits.after: This is where Warwick takes over. At 2+ items Jaws of the Beast and lifesteal off your bar out-sustain your burst, so Grievous Wounds is the item that keeps you in the fight, and Infinite Duress locks you for his team if you dive first. Use E mobility and R isolation to pick a SQUISHY carry rather than duelling him — and remember your Hookshot knockup breaks a Duress channel on a teammate. Close the game before his sustain outweighs your picks.

notes: Slot error: Warwick's fear was attributed to Blood Hunt (W) twice when it is Primal Howl (E). That hid a 15s ability behind an 80s one and left out Primal Howl's damage reduction, which is the real reason a clean Camille burst fails to kill him. Blood Hunt itself was written as a steroid that comes 'online' when it is an 80s-at-rank-1 cooldown — the most punishable cooldown in the lane by a wide margin. Added the interaction _missing-interactions.json flags for this pairing: Hookshot's landing knockup interrupts the Infinite Duress channel, which Camille cannot use on herself while suppressed but is her best peel tool for a teammate. Grievous Wounds was absent despite six lines blaming his healing.
